jobs.occupation: Biologe (m/w/d) (Biologe/Biologin)
jobs.description: We are seeking a highly motivated PhD candidate to join our Systems Biology Department at the Institute of Biomedical Genetics (IBMG), University of Stuttgart (https://www.ibmg.uni-stuttgart.de/systems_biology/). The successful applicant will study the regulatory mechanisms of alternative splicing in health and disease using a combination of kinetic modeling, bioinformatic data analysis and/or AI. The appointment will initially be limited to 3 years.The University of Stuttgart is one of the leading technical universities in Germany and provides an inspiring interdisciplinary environment at the interface of biology and engineering. The Systems Biology group combines mathematical modelling with state-of-the-art experimentation and is part of the newly founded Institute for Biomedical Genetics as well as the Stuttgart Research Center Systems Biology (SRCSB), one of the largest German interfaculty infrastructures for systems biological research (https://www.srscsb.uni-stuttgart.de/).A core focus of our group is the quantitative investigation of alternative splicing, a fundamental regulatory mechanism essential for maintaining normal cellular physiology and development, while its dysregulation often leads to disease pathogenesis and therapy resistance. Combining multi-omics profiling, mechanistic modeling, and machine learning, we have derived quantitative principles governing how alternative splicing is regulated by cis- and trans-acting factors, genetic variants and cellular context (see e.g., Kristofori et al., Nucleic Acids Research 2026; Li et al., Cell Systems in press; Prieto-Garcia et al., Science 2024; Cortés-López et al., Nature Communications 2022; Enculescu et al., Biophysical Journal 2020; Braun et al., Nature Communications 2018). We will continue to apply this integrated strategy to dissect disease-relevant splicing perturbations, with a particular focus on cancers and disorders linked to defects in splicing machinery components.in splicing machinery components.We offerA PhD student position initially for 3 years (65% E13)Interdisciplinary education within the SRCSB, the SimTech excellence cluster (https://www.simtech.uni-stuttgart.de/) and the Graduate Academy of the University of Stuttgart (https://www.gradus.uni-stuttgart.de/en/)Priority access to high-performance computing resourcesA vibrant, interdisciplinary, and collaborative research environmentDevelop quantitative models of alternative splicing regulation providing mechanistic insights into perturbed splicing decisions and splicing fidelity in cancer cells (see e.g., Kristofori et al., Nucleic Acids Research 2026; Prieto-Garcia et al., Science 2024; Braun et al., Nature Communications 2018)Process raw sequencing data (e.g., short- and long-read RNA sequencing), then perform comprehensive downstream analyses and data visualizationEmploy machine learning and AI techniques to train kinetic models on quantitative experimental data.Collaborate closely with experimentalists and theoreticians within or outside the groupParticipate in teaching in systems biologyMaster's degree (or equivalent) in computational biology, bioinformatics, physics, mathematics, molecular biology, informatics, or a related fieldStrong skills in programming and numerical computation, e.g., Matlab, Python, R or JuliaEnthusiasm for basic research questions and the ability to solve problems independentlyExcellent communication skills and good team spiritFluency in spoken and written EnglishExperience in quantitative systems biology research, particularly in the context of RNA biology or alternative splicing, is beneficialPlease send a single PDF file containing:A motivation letter including a description of previous research experiencesA full CVA list of publications (if applicable)Scans of academic degrees (e.g. Abitur & Master degree)Contact details of two refereesStarting dateAs soon as possibleClosing dateApplications will be ...
